DopMenu Privacy policy Support

Privacy policy

DopMenu · Effective 18 October 2026

DopMenu collects no data. What it keeps stays on your Mac, and it never connects to the internet.

In short

  • DopMenu collects no data. The app sends nothing you do in it to me or to anyone else.
  • It never connects to the internet.
  • It has no accounts, no analytics of its own, no ads and no tracking.
  • What it keeps stays on your Mac, in its own folder, and you can delete it at any time.
  • Apple, which runs the Mac App Store, may share some statistics and crash reports with me: see What Apple may share with me.

Who makes DopMenu

DopMenu is a personal menu of activities in the Mac menu bar. It is made by one person, Roman Elosvili, as an individual developer. “I” and “me” on this page mean the developer. You can write to me about anything on this page at dopmenu.app@gmail.com.

What stays on your Mac

To work, DopMenu keeps these on your Mac:

  • the activities in your list, with their time, energy, icon, tag, note and times a day, when each was added, changed or removed, and your list of tags
  • each Did it, with its date, time and time zone
  • what you snoozed, with the day
  • the timers that ran to the end, with their dates, and the timer running now
  • your choices in Settings, and the time and energy you chose last
  • your answers to the welcome questions, if DopMenu asked them when it first opened
  • where you put its menu bar icon, and the size and place of its windows

They are kept in DopMenu's own folder, which macOS keeps for it alone: ~/Library/Containers/com.romane002.DopamineMenu. DopMenu keeps these until you delete them, and keeps nothing of yours anywhere else on your Mac.

Your list and your history are in two files: ~/Library/Containers/com.romane002.DopamineMenu/Data/Library/Application Support/Dopamine Menu/state.json, and state.last-good.json beside it, a copy of the last good save that DopMenu uses if the first file is ever damaged. If a file cannot be read, DopMenu keeps it there under a new name, so nothing is lost. macOS saves the icon's place and the window sizes elsewhere in DopMenu's own folder, among its preferences.

DopMenu sends nothing in this folder anywhere, and it has no syncing: each Mac keeps its own. If you back up your Mac, for example with Time Machine, the backup may include this folder.

Outside this folder, macOS keeps its own settings for DopMenu: whether it may show notifications, and Launch at login if you turned it on. DopMenu notifications you have not cleared stay in Notification Centre. If DopMenu ever crashes, macOS keeps a crash report in ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports.

No internet, no tracking

DopMenu never connects to the internet. It runs in Apple's App Sandbox and does not have the permission a sandboxed app needs to use the network.

It has no accounts, no sign-in, no analytics, no ads and no tracking, and it contains no analytics or advertising code from anyone.

It does not ask for access to your files, contacts, calendars, location, camera or microphone. It asks to show notifications only when you click Allow in its Settings.

Its notifications are made on your Mac: “Session finished”, which names the activity, and a note if its menu bar icon is hidden behind the notch. DopMenu asks macOS to show them, and the chime is a sound inside the app. You can turn DopMenu's notifications off at any time in System Settings → Notifications.

In DopMenu, Privacy policy and Support open these pages in your web browser. The browser loads them; DopMenu itself does not.

What Apple may share with me

DopMenu is distributed through Apple's Mac App Store. Apple handles the download, and your Apple Account, under Apple's privacy policy.

Apple shows me statistics from the App Store, such as how many times DopMenu was downloaded, by day and by country or region.

If you have agreed on your Mac to share analytics with app developers, Apple may also share with me statistics about how DopMenu is used, and reports of its crashes. Apple includes only people who agreed to share, and shows the usage statistics only once enough people are counted. On a Mac, this choice is in System Settings, under Privacy & Security, then Analytics & Improvements. You can turn it off there at any time.

Apple keeps this information under its own privacy policy. I use it only to see how many people use DopMenu and to fix crashes.

If you write to me

If you email dopmenu.app@gmail.com, your email address and your message reach a Gmail mailbox that I use only for DopMenu. Gmail is run by Google, under Google's privacy policy.

I use your message only to answer you, and I never sell it or pass it on. I keep your messages in that mailbox while I support DopMenu, and I delete them sooner if you ask.

These web pages

These pages are hosted by GitHub Pages. When you open them, GitHub logs and keeps your IP address for security purposes, as its GitHub Pages documentation says, and handles it under the GitHub General Privacy Statement.

The pages themselves use no cookies, no scripts and no web fonts, and they load nothing from other websites.

Deleting your data

DopMenu has no button that erases everything at once. Removing an activity hides it from your list but keeps it in the file, with what you already did with it, so your history stays whole.

To delete everything DopMenu has kept on your Mac:

  1. If you turned on Launch at login, turn it off in DopMenu's Settings.
  2. Quit DopMenu: open its panel and click Quit at the bottom.
  3. In Finder, open Applications and move DopMenu to the Trash.
  4. In Finder, choose Go → Go to Folder…, type ~/Library/Containers/ and press Return.
  5. Find DopMenu's folder there: Finder may show it as DopMenu, and its real name is com.romane002.DopamineMenu. Move it to the Trash.
  6. Clear any DopMenu notifications in Notification Centre.
  7. Empty the Trash.

Moving the app to the Trash on its own leaves this folder in place. Backups you made earlier may still hold a copy.

To have your emails to me deleted, write to dopmenu.app@gmail.com.

Changes to this policy

If this policy changes, the new version is published on this page with a new effective date. Earlier versions stay visible in the page's public history.

What DopMenu does on your Mac can change only with an update from the Mac App Store. If an update ever changed what DopMenu keeps or sends, this policy and the App Store's privacy details would change before that update is released.
